title: Story Characters
objectives: I can name eight traits that tell what a character is like.
I can prove a trait with something the character says or does.
I can use one exact trait word instead of nice or mean.
I can tell how a character changes or stays the same in a story.
rationale: Character traits like nice and mean are too broad to show what a character is really like. These eight traits are more exact, so children can support an idea about a character with one word and one piece of proof from the story. The words split into how a character treats others (generous, loyal, cheerful), how a character faces new things (bold, shy, determined), and how a character acts when others disagree or are not watching (stubborn, sneaky). The unit revisits jealous, foolish, trick, and journey because these are the feelings, choices, and story parts that traits explain.

words.def: Happy to give or share with others.
words.ex: The generous baker gave bread to every neighbor.
words.ex2: Mia was generous and shared her crayons with the class.
words.nonExample: Keeping every toy for yourself is not generous.

apps.academic: A generous character gives time, help, or things.
apps.spoken: That was generous of you to share.
apps.writing: Use generous and tell what the character gave.

cloze.s: The ___ girl gave half of her lunch to a hungry friend.

cloze2.s: It was ___ of Mr. Cho to give every child a free book.

misuse.s: The generous boy hid all his toys and would not share one.
misuse.why: A generous person shares, so hiding toys is the opposite.

visual.alt: Two open hands holding out a gift.

words.def: Not willing to change your mind.
words.ex: The stubborn donkey would not move from the road.
words.ex2: Ben was stubborn and kept saying no to every idea.
words.nonExample: A person who listens and changes a plan is not stubborn.

apps.academic: A stubborn character may cause a problem in a story.
apps.writing: Use stubborn when a character refuses to change even when there is a good reason.

cloze.s: The ___ mule sat down and refused to walk, even when we pulled the rope.

cloze2.s: Do not be so ___; try the new game once before you say no.

misuse.s: She was stubborn, so she quickly changed her mind every time someone asked.
misuse.why: A stubborn person does not change her mind easily.

visual.alt: A goat standing still beside a child shaking her head.

words.def: Always true to a friend or a promise.
words.ex: The loyal dog waited at the door all day for his boy.
words.ex2: A loyal friend stays with you when things are hard.
words.nonExample: A friend who leaves when things get hard is not loyal.

apps.academic: A loyal character stays on a friend's side.
apps.writing: Use loyal and tell how the character showed it.

cloze.s: The ___ dog stayed by his owner's side during the whole storm.

cloze2.s: A ___ friend will keep your secret and help you when you are sad.

misuse.s: A loyal friend leaves you alone whenever you need help.
misuse.why: A loyal friend stays and helps, so leaving is the opposite.

visual.alt: A dog sitting beside a child who holds out a hand.

words.ex: The cheerful bus driver greeted every child with a smile.
words.ex2: Ana stayed cheerful even on the rainy day.
words.nonExample: A grumpy person with a frown is not cheerful.

apps.academic: A cheerful character helps others feel good.
apps.spoken: She is always cheerful in the morning.
apps.writing: Use cheerful with a word like smiled or sang to show the trait.

cloze.s: The ___ girl hummed a song and waved at everyone on the street.

cloze2.s: Even on a cold, gray morning, Leo felt ___ and ready to play.

misuse.s: The cheerful boy cried all day and frowned at every person.
misuse.why: A cheerful person is happy, so crying and frowning is the opposite.

visual.alt: A smiling face beside a bright sun.

words.def: Brave and not afraid to try new things.
words.ex: The bold girl walked up to the stage and sang.
words.ex2: The bold kitten jumped onto the big dog's back.
words.nonExample: Hiding behind a door is not bold.
words.rel: how a character faces new things

apps.academic: A bold character takes a chance.
apps.writing: Use bold and tell the brave thing the character did.

cloze.s: The ___ knight rode up to the dragon without fear.

cloze2.s: It was ___ of Jo to ask the principal a question in front of everyone.

misuse.s: The bold mouse was so afraid that she ran and hid under the bed.
misuse.why: A bold character is brave, so running to hide is the opposite.

visual.alt: A hero with a cape beside a lion.

words.frame: A bold character is not afraid to ___.

words.def: Nervous around people you do not know.
words.ex: The shy boy hid behind his mother at first.
words.ex2: Lia was shy, but she smiled when she met the new girl.
words.nonExample: A child who loves to speak to a crowd is not shy.
words.rel: how a character faces new things

apps.academic: A shy character may need time to feel safe.
apps.spoken: He is shy around new people.
apps.writing: Use shy and tell what the character did when meeting someone.

cloze.s: The ___ kitten hid under the couch when visitors came.

cloze2.s: On the first day of school, Rosa felt ___ and did not say a word.

misuse.s: The shy girl loudly shouted hello to a huge crowd and loved it.
misuse.why: A shy person is nervous around new people, so shouting to a crowd is the opposite.

visual.alt: A girl covering her eyes with her hands.

words.def: Doing things quietly so others will not notice.
words.ex: The sneaky fox crept past the sleeping dog.
words.ex2: A sneaky boy took an extra cookie when no one looked.
words.nonExample: Asking for a cookie out loud is not sneaky.

apps.academic: A sneaky character hides what he is doing.
apps.writing: Use sneaky for a character who acts when no one is watching.

cloze.s: The ___ raccoon tiptoed into the camp and took a snack when no one was looking.

cloze2.s: It is ___ to hide a frog in your sister's shoe.

misuse.s: The sneaky boy announced loudly that he was taking the cookie.
misuse.why: A sneaky person hides what he is doing, so announcing it loudly is the opposite.

visual.alt: A raccoon holding a finger to its lips.

words.def: Not giving up; set on reaching a goal.
words.ex: The determined girl kept practicing until she could ride her bike.
words.ex2: A determined ant carried the crumb up the hill.
words.nonExample: Giving up after one try is not being determined.
words.rel: how a character faces new things

apps.writing: Use determined and tell the goal the character wanted.

cloze.s: The ___ runner finished the race even though her legs were tired.

cloze2.s: Be ___ to finish your puzzle, even if it is hard.

misuse.s: The determined boy quit after one try and never tried again.
misuse.why: A determined person does not give up, so quitting after one try is the opposite.

visual.alt: A strong arm beside a finish flag.

passage.title: Pip and Dot
paras: Pip was a cheerful goat, and Dot was a shy sheep. They were loyal friends. A sneaky fox came to take their corn.
Pip was bold, and he was determined to guard the garden. He was not stubborn, so he asked Dot for ideas. Then generous Dot gave the fox a carrot, and the fox went home.

qs.q: What does "sneaky" mean in the story?
qs.why: The fox came to take their corn, and a sneaky character acts quietly so no one notices.

qs.q: What did Dot do to make the fox go home?
qs.why: The story says generous Dot gave the fox a carrot.
Dot was shy and gave the fox a carrot, so she was shy and generous.

study.task: Choose a character from a book you know. Pick one trait word from the unit. Write the word, one thing the character did, and one thing the character said.

Write a sentence about a time someone was generous.

constructed.prompt: Tell how a character in a story showed one of these traits. Use generous or loyal.
look: connects the action to the trait

teacher.overview: Children learn eight traits that are more exact than nice or mean, and use them to describe characters with proof from the text. Use a trait chart with the word, the proof, and a sentence. Revisit jealous, foolish, trick, and journey to explain why a character acts as he or she does.

notes.va.generous.adj: Generous is about giving or sharing, not only money. Ask what a character gave: time, help, food. Cognate generoso.
notes.va.stubborn.adj: Stubborn is not always bad. Ask whether the character should have changed her mind. Contrast with determined: stubborn refuses to change; determined keeps trying toward a goal.
notes.va.loyal.adj: Loyal means staying true to a person or a promise. Use dogs and friend stories. Ask how the character showed it when things got hard.
notes.va.cheerful.adj: Cheerful is happy and showing it. Different from happy: cheerful is a trait that lasts, and happy can be a moment. Use a face or a voice.
notes.va.bold.adj: Bold means brave and willing to try. A bold character is not always wise; link to the foolish and wise words from fables. Spanish: audaz or valiente.
notes.va.shy.adj: Shy is not a weakness. Teach it with kindness and use story characters only. Contrast with bold. Shy characters can be loyal and generous too.
notes.va.sneaky.adj: Sneaky means acting so no one notices, often to do something unkind. A sneaky character may play a trick. Spanish: furtivo or taimado depending on region.
notes.va.determined.adj: Determined means set on a goal and not giving up. Use stories where a character fails and tries again. Cognate determinado.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'The text says the fox crept in so no one would see. That is a clue. A character who acts quietly so no one notices is sneaky. I can prove it with the clue that he crept in.'
discuss: Which trait word best fits a character in a book you know? What is your proof?
Can a character have two traits at once?
misconceptions: Children may think every trait is good or bad. Traits like stubborn and shy depend on the story.
Some children say a character is shy and loyal as one idea. Separate each trait with its own proof.
Children may name a trait without proof; always ask what did the character do or say?
extend: Make a trait web for a character with each trait and its proof.
Act out a short scene and have the class name the trait.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit jealous, foolish, trick, and journey: a jealous character may be sneaky, a foolish choice may come from being stubborn, and a bold character may go on a journey.

frames: I know he is ___ because he ___.
wida.oral: Pick a character. Tell your partner a trait word and one thing the character did to prove it.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (generoso, terco, leal, alegre, audaz, tímido, furtivo, decidido) not reviewed by a native speaker; sneaky has regional options such as taimado or solapado.
The passage names an invented fox, goat, and sheep; no animal facts are claimed.
